title: The reviewer experience, and the team's first hour on its own
headline: All nine members now run on their own, every two hours, after you approved five scheduled tasks; nothing waits on you to keep working. In their first hour: RC1 is in the manuscript (259 pages), the PDF lab printed LAB 01 and its first experiment, 21 more numbers are registered, and the storyteller proposed plan draft 6. Your new project, the reviewer experience, has a brief, two new members drafted (developer@, synthetic@) and two decisions for you (R1, R2).

sections.title: The reviewer experience in one paragraph
sections.text: One link per reviewer, theirs alone: the personal part travels in the URL's fragment, which never reaches a server. It opens a page that knows why we asked them, what to read (three chapters, about forty minutes) and the questions. Every paragraph takes a pen mark; comments go to you encrypted. When a revision ships, they see what their comments changed. Beside each step, one line on how the technology works, which is the showcase. First built with fictional data and tested by eight synthetic readers; then you; then one friendly reviewer; then the first wave.
